Subject: Hosted API pricing: commit tiers & burst options

Hi Ellis,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — really enjoyed the conversation and the product fit looks strong. Attached is a concise pricing proposal keyed to your forecast (see the attached pricing-proposal.pdf). High-level summary:

- Commit tiers: three levels (Standard / Scale / Enterprise) with stepwise per-token discounts as commit increases.
- Minimum monthly commit: proposal starts at $15k/mo as the baseline for the Scale tier.
- Overage (on-demand over commit): bill at a premium multiplier vs commit rate (we proposed 1.6x).
- Burst: short-term bursts (up to 25% above committed quota in a billing period) at a higher on-demand rate (proposed 1.9x) to ensure predictable capacity for spikes.

Questions I expect from procurement: minimum term, early-termination, and exact per-token maths. If you want, we can produce a worked example based on your March forecast.

Next steps: if the high-level looks reasonable, I can loop in our Sales Director (Neha) and Finance (Aditya) to firm up legal/PO flow and draft DocuSign terms.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the doc. A few items from our finance and infra teams:

1) Minimum monthly commit — $15k is higher than we anticipated. Can you do $10k/mo as the floor for Scale?
2) Overage/On-demand rate — 1.6x feels steep for large spikes. Can that be 1.3x, at least within the first 10% over commit?
3) Burst treatment — we need clearer guarantees that bursts won’t be rate-limited. If you cap bursts at 25% above commit please confirm both rate and enforcement policy.

I attached our forecast (brightai-forecast.xlsx) so you can see month-by-month expected tokens. If you can send a worked example (per-token math for our Q2) and a mutual action plan, we can move this quickly.

Cheers,
Ellis
Head of Product, BrightAI
ellis@brightai.io

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: commit tiers & burst options

Ellis —

Appreciate the clear asks and the forecast — that helps a lot. Quick answers up front, then a proposed compromise:

1) Minimum monthly commit: we can flex to $12k/mo for a 12-month committed term (we typically require 12 months for that floor).
2) Overage structure: propose a two-band model:
   - First 10% over commit: 1.4x of the committed unit rate
   - Anything beyond 10% in the billing period: 1.8x (this preserves headroom and prevents runaway exposure)
3) Burst guarantees: bursts up to 25% will be allowed and routed to on-demand capacity; we can include a short SLO in the contract that prioritizes capacity for burst windows but at the higher on-demand rate. If you need hard capacity reservations for sustained spikes, Dedicated capacity is the better route.

To make this concrete, attached is a redlines.xlsx that maps the per-token math using one of your months from the forecast. Summary example (rounded):
- Committed unit price (Scale tier): $0.0008 per token with $12k/month commit -> ~15M tokens included.
- 8% overage in a month (~1.2M tokens): billed at 1.4x -> $0.0008 * 1.4 * 1.2M = ~$1,344 extra.
- 30% spike (beyond the 25% burst cap): the excess beyond burst threshold billed at 1.8x until the end of the billing period.

If that looks workable we can: 1) lock the floor at $12k/mo; 2) offer a 10% introductory discount off the committed unit rate for year 1 (to help your ramp); 3) include the two-band overage model.

Neha/Aditya — tagging you for finance confirmation and legal cadence.

-Jordan

- Procurement: can we get explicit per-token tables for three volume tiers (15M, 50M, 150M tokens) showing committed price, first-10%-overage price, >10% overage price, and effective blended price at sample utilization points? That makes approvals faster.
- Infra: can you include a short note on how bursts are detected and any soft throttling behavior (we need assurance we won't get partial responses under load).

I'll also need a mutual action plan with dates (trial, PO, signature, kickoff) — if you draft that we can align.

Thanks,
Ellis

Quick internal: finance reviewed Jordan's proposed compromise. We can approve discussion-level terms below but do NOT sign anything outside these guardrails without VP sign-off:

- Max promotional discount: 12% off committed unit rate for year-1 (Jordan suggested 10% — OK to go to 12% if needed).
- Minimum monthly commit floor: no lower than $12k/mo for a 12-month term.
- Two-band overage model is OK (1.4x first 10%, 1.8x thereafter).
- Burst up to 25% allowed; we should include a short note in SOW that sustained >25% in two consecutive months triggers review and potential upgrade to Dedicated.

Jordan — proceed to produce the per-token tables and a 4-step mutual action plan; once Ellis confirms we push DocuSign (use the HubSpot deal above). Aditya — confirm if the initial PO can be net-30 and whether we need a pre-bill for the first month.

-Neha

Ellis —

Thanks for the clarifying asks. Per Neha's internal approval, here's a consolidated final offer and a short mutual action plan (MAP). I attached a one-page final-pricing-offer.pdf with the tables; key points below.

Final commercial terms (summary)
- Commit tier (Scale): $0.0008 per token base, $12,000/month minimum for a 12-month term.
- Intro discount: 10% off committed unit price for Year 1 (can move to 12% with redline request but would require sales director sign-off).
- Overage (on-demand over commit):
   * First 10% over commit in a billing period: 1.4x committed unit rate
   * Beyond 10%: 1.8x committed unit rate
- Burst: up to 25% temporary burst allowed; bursts routed to on-demand pool, billed at the on-demand multiplier above. Sustained >25% in two consecutive months triggers a commercial review and recommendation for Dedicated capacity.
- Billing: Net-30, standard SOW and Master Services Agreement.

Worked examples (from your forecast) are in the attached PDF. Quick sample: for a month with 15M included tokens, an 8% overage (~1.2M tokens) would be billed at 1.4x -> incremental charge approx $1.3k.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP)
1) Trial + final validation (this week): BrightAI runs test workload against hosted endpoint (we will provide console access and a support onboarding session). Target: Mar 26.
2) Purchase order and sign (BrightAI): procurement submits PO and signs DocuSign. Target: Apr 2.
3) Kickoff & onboarding: initial architectural review + SLOs. Target: Apr 5.
4) Post-commit review: 45 days after go-live to confirm utilization and evaluate if Dedicated makes sense.
